title: GAAI portable pre-merge proof contract
description: Three named schemas: $defs/trust_manifest (base-held policy, read from the base commit B, never from a PR copy), $defs/evidence (the untrusted, caller-supplied description of a CI run) and $defs/verdict (the full merge-proof verdict a verifier emits after independently resolving Git state and cross-checking the evidence). Consumers reference a fragment, e.g. premerge-policy.schema.json#/$defs/trust_manifest. A verifier resolves this document only from B, at .gaai/core/ci/premerge-policy.schema.json, so a candidate can never weaken the contract that judges it.

reason_enum.description: Stable, closed terminal-reason taxonomy. The verifier checks in one fixed order so a verdict never reports two simultaneous causes; the same ordered list is restated behind the same marker in the verifier library header, and the two must stay equal. PRIORITY_ORDER: environment_error, schema_invalid, identity_mode_conflict, commit_unresolvable, parent_mismatch, tuple_forged, tree_mismatch, manifest_digest_mismatch, provenance_mismatch, policy_missing, trust_surface_changed, run_attempt_mismatch, job_missing, job_duplicate, job_not_success

workflow_identity.description: Identity of the single validation workflow this policy trusts. A default policy may forward-declare the managed workflow the installation change will create, before that file exists; the identity is declared here and never listed in covered_paths, because a covered path matching nothing at B is policy_missing. The change that creates the workflow must create exactly this identity and add its own new trust surfaces, the workflow file included, to covered_paths.

path.description: Repository-relative path of the trusted validation workflow.

name.description: Workflow name as declared in the workflow file.

trust_manifest.title: trust_manifest
trust_manifest.description: Versioned JSON trust manifest, resolvable only from the base commit B. Defines schema/policy versions, digest algorithm, workflow identity, trust-covered paths, the complete required-job set, the validation profile, and an optional rollover approval reference.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the manifest instance conforms to (e.g. "1.0.0").

policy_version.description: Version of the policy content itself, independent of schema_version.

digest_algorithm.description: Canonical digest algorithm. Closed to sha256 in this schema version.

covered_paths.description: Repository-relative paths that must be byte-identical between the base commit B and the synthetic merge commit T for the base to remain a trust root (AC3). Every entry must be one canonical literal path resolving to a real object at B: absolute paths, empty or dot components, parent-directory components, trailing separators, embedded newline or NUL bytes, Git pathspec magic (a leading colon) and glob metacharacters are rejected, since none of them denote one unambiguous auditable object.

required_jobs.description: The complete set of job names that must each appear exactly once with a successful conclusion (AC5). A repeated name here violates this published uniqueItems constraint and is schema_invalid; a repeated job name in evidence is job_duplicate instead, because that is untrusted run data rather than policy.

validation_profile.description: Identifier of the validation profile this manifest enforces (e.g. "standard").

rollover_approval_ref.description: Optional reference (e.g. a human-approval artefact or commit) authorizing a change to this manifest's own trust-covered content. Declared here and intentionally left unread by the verifier; binding it to a current human approval decision belongs to the merge-authorization layer.

base_ref.description: Untrusted ref selector resolved locally to B. The merge-authorization layer must bind it to the controller-resolved repository base before this proof can authorize a merge.

head_ref.description: Untrusted ref selector resolved locally to H. The merge-authorization layer must bind it to the controller-resolved current candidate head.

merge_group_ref.description: Untrusted ref selector for the merge-group candidate; controller binding remains an authorization-layer duty.

base_ref.description: Untrusted ref selector resolved locally to B. The merge-authorization layer must bind it to the controller-resolved repository base before this proof can authorize a merge.

run_identity.description: Identity of the CI run that produced the evidence. workflow_path and workflow_name are compared against the base-held manifest's workflow identity and event must equal the mode, so a run of another workflow — or of the trusted workflow under a different trigger — cannot be presented as this proof (provenance_mismatch).

evidence.title: evidence
evidence.description: Caller-supplied, untrusted description of a CI run. Every identity, commit and tree claim it carries is independently recomputed from Git and cross-checked; nothing here is taken at face value. Closed field set: x_extensions is the single tolerated top-level extension point and any other unrecognized key is schema_invalid, never silently ignored.

repository.description: owner/repo the run claims. Carried into the verdict and deliberately not verified at this layer: binding it to a controller-resolved repository identity belongs to the merge-authorization layer.

identity.description: Mode-shaped identity block. Matching neither published shape is schema_invalid; matching the other mode's shape is identity_mode_conflict, evaluated only after structural validation.

merge_ref.description: Untrusted Git ref selector resolved locally to T; the merge-authorization layer binds the resulting tuple to the current controller-resolved candidate.

jobs.description: Observed jobs. Deliberately not uniqueItems: a duplicated required job name is ambiguous run evidence (job_duplicate), not a malformed document.

x_extensions.description: The single explicitly-allowed extension point on evidence. Free-form; not validated further.

verdict.title: verdict
verdict.description: Full merge-proof verdict binding repository, PR-or-merge-group identity, B/H/T/tree(T), workflow/run identity, run_attempt, event, manifest digest, validation profile, and every required job (AC4). A rejection raised before the evidence has been structurally validated carries null in every data field instead of echoing unvalidated input, so every verdict the verifier can emit — on success and on every rejection path — validates against this schema.

repository.description: owner/repo the verdict applies to; null before evidence validation.

mode.description: Provenance mode. A merge_group verdict cannot be confused with a pull_request verdict (AC2).

identity.description: Mode-shaped identity block, or null before evidence validation.

merge_sha.description: T — resolved synthetic merge commit; parents(T) == (B, H) in order for pull_request mode.

tree_sha.description: tree(T) — the tree object of the synthetic merge commit.

manifest_digest.description: Canonical sha256 digest of the trust_manifest read from B.

x_extensions.description: The single explicitly-allowed schema extension point on verdict (AC4). Free-form; not validated further.
